question: Which Governor-General is correctly matched with the policy followed during his tenure?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Wellesley – Expansionist policy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Cornwallis – Subsidiary Alliance:** The statement is incorrect. The Subsidiary Alliance policy was introduced by **Lord Wellesley**, not Lord Cornwallis. Lord Cornwallis is better known for his administrative reforms, particularly the **Permanent Settlement system** in Bengal.
 
• **Lord Wellesley – Expansionist policy:** This is the correct match. Lord Wellesley (1798–1805) pursued an aggressive **expansionist policy** by introducing the Subsidiary Alliance system. Through this policy, Indian princely states were required to accept British protection and maintain British troops at their expense, leading to significant territorial annexations.
 
• **Lord Hastings – Doctrine of Lapse:** The statement is incorrect. The Doctrine of Lapse was introduced by **Lord Dalhousie**, not Lord Hastings. Lord Hastings (1813–1823) is known for his consolidation of British power, including victories in the Third Anglo-Maratha War.
 
• **Warren Hastings – Anti-imperialism:** The statement is incorrect. Warren Hastings (1772–1785) was the first Governor-General of Bengal and laid the foundation of British administration in India. He was not known for any anti-imperialistic stance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lord Wellesley:**

 
 
• He served as the **Governor-General of India from 1798 to 1805**.
 
• Introduced the **Subsidiary Alliance** system, which was a key component of his expansionist policy.
 
• The Subsidiary Alliance system ensured that Indian states maintained British troops and surrendered foreign policy control to the British. States like **Hyderabad, Mysore, Tanjore, and Awadh** came under this policy.
 
• He annexed territories like **Mysore** (1799) and expanded British influence across India.
 
 
 
• **Lord Cornwallis:**
 
 
• Served as **Governor-General from 1786 to 1793**.
 
• Introduced the **Permanent Settlement system** in Bengal, fixing land revenue with zamindars.
 
• Reformed civil services, emphasizing merit-based recruitment and integrity.
 
 
 
• **Lord Hastings:**
 
 
• Served as **Governor-General from 1813 to 1823**.
 
• Known for the defeat of the Marathas in the **Third Anglo-Maratha War** (1817–1818), which marked the end of Maratha power.
 
• Played a role in the expansion of British territories in India.
 
 
 
• **Warren Hastings:**
 
 
• Served as the first **Governor-General of Bengal from 1772 to 1785**.
 
• Reorganized the revenue system and judicial structure in Bengal.
 
• Facilitated the translation of Hindu and Muslim laws to aid British administration.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Subsidiary Alliance:** Introduced by **Lord Wellesley**, this policy required Indian rulers to accept British troops in their territory and pay for their maintenance.
 
• **Doctrine of Lapse:** Introduced by **Lord Dalhousie**, this policy allowed the British to annex any princely state without a male heir.
 
• **Permanent Settlement:** Introduced by **Lord Cornwallis**, this system fixed land revenue and created a class of zamindars in Bengal.
 
• **Anglo-Maratha Wars:** Fought during the tenure of **Lord Hastings**, leading to the dissolution of Maratha power.
